question: How was midwifery knowledge primarily passed down in ancient times?

options.A: Orally from one generation to the next

explanation: Before formal schools existed, experienced women shared their trade by word of mouth and practical demonstration with younger women in the community. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which statement best describes how ancient societies viewed childbirth?

options.A: As an illness that required prolonged bed rest in a ward
options.B: As a surgical procedure requiring a team of doctors
options.C: As a natural and domestic event managed by women
options.D: As an administrative duty handled by village leaders

explanation: Childbirth took place at home and was treated as a normal part of life handled by female community members rather than a disease managed in a hospital. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h1)

question: Where did the shift in childbirth take place during the 18th and 19th centuries in the West?

options.A: From hospitals back to private homes
options.B: From community centers to open-air markets
options.C: From homes into formal medical institutions
options.D: From herbalist huts to spiritual shrines

explanation: The Western medical movement brought laboring women out of their domestic environments and into hospitals for delivery. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h2)

question: What was a major consequence of the medicalization of childbirth in Western history?

options.A: Pregnancy became entirely free of any complications
options.B: Childbirth was increasingly treated as a medical condition
options.C: Hospitals stopped using surgical instruments entirely
options.D: Traditional midwives gained higher social status

explanation: As doctors took over maternity care, normal labor began to be viewed and managed as an illness or medical event needing intervention. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h2)

question: Who typically served as the primary maternity care providers in pre-colonial Nigerian communities?
explanation: Respected community women, known as Traditional Birth Attendants, provided the frontline support for pregnant women across indigenous Nigerian societies. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote pre-colonial setting needed comfort during labor. What intervention was most likely used by her local birth attendant?
explanation: Indigenous care relied on natural remedies, physical comfort measures like massage, and traditional support systems rather than modern medical technology. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h3)

question: What was the primary initial purpose of introducing Western medicine during the early colonial era in Nigeria?

options.A: To completely eliminate all herbal medicine
options.B: To establish free university hospitals nationwide
options.C: To train local villagers in advanced surgery
options.D: To care for colonial officers and expatriates

explanation: Western medical services were initially brought in to protect the health of British administrators and foreign workers stationed in the territory. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h4)

question: How did the arrival of colonial health services affect maternity care in Nigeria?

options.A: It forced every pregnant woman to give birth in Europe
options.B: It immediately ended all maternal mortality across the country
options.C: It introduced formal training schools and Western delivery techniques
options.D: It completely integrated traditional birth practices into medical boards

explanation: Missionaries and colonial authorities set up the first maternity homes and began training local women in Western-style midwifery concepts. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h4)

question: What major shift occurred in midwifery education in Nigeria after independence in 1960?

options.A: Education was moved entirely out of hospitals and into factories
options.B: Training became strictly based on informal apprenticeships
options.C: Curricula were formalized and aligned with structured institutions
options.D: All midwifery schools were closed down by the government

explanation: The post-independence era focused on building organized educational programs with standardized curricula to train Nigerian healthcare workers. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why were post-independence health reforms necessary for Nigerian nursing and midwifery?

options.A: To replace foreign personnel with trained indigenous professionals
options.B: To ban all forms of traditional remedies from the country
options.C: To reduce the number of hospitals operating in rural areas
options.D: To make healthcare entirely dependent on foreign grants

explanation: A newly independent nation needed its own qualified local workforce to run hospitals, maternity centers, and public health programs effectively. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which organization is legally responsible for registering and disciplining midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body established to control and regulate the education and practice of the profession. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary function of professional associations such as the National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives?

options.A: To build private commercial hospitals across the country
options.B: To set legal penalties for criminal offenses in courts
options.C: To advocate for worker welfare and uphold professional ethics
options.D: To import pharmaceutical drugs from overseas manufacturers

explanation: Professional associations exist to protect the interests of their members, promote high ethical standards, and support professional growth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a major challenge faced by modern midwives working in various parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Having too many doctors and no patients to care for
options.B: Bridging global standards with local infrastructural gaps
options.C: The complete absence of pregnant women in rural areas
options.D: An absolute surplus of high-tech maternity hospitals

explanation: Midwives must strive to deliver high-quality global care standards even when working in facilities that may lack basic equipment or steady power. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h7)

question: A midwife is posted to a rural primary health center with limited equipment and high maternal mortality. What approach best reflects the modern role of the midwife in this setting?

options.A: Referrals only, offering no primary care services on-site
options.B: Combining clinical care with public health education and advocacy
options.C: Focusing solely on routine deliveries without community outreach
options.D: Refusing to work until a major surgical theater is built

explanation: Modern midwives act as educators and public health leaders who actively engage their communities to improve health outcomes despite resource limits. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h7)
